title: Article: Concept Of Multiple Astral Bodies And Kuldevta

segments.text: Can Kaliyug Make You More Powerful Than Satyug? The Shocking Truth Behind This Age

It’s commonly believed that people in Satyug lived longer and were spiritually stronger. While that’s partly true, there’s another side to the story—in Kalyug, despite shorter lifespans, we have the potential to become spiritually more powerful.
Let’s understand how, with a real and fascinating example.
Meet Baba Ramdev Peer – A Divine Avatar in Kalyug
Baba Ramdev Peer, also known as a Kuldevta for many, was a powerful incarnation of Lord Vishnu—just like Lord Rama and Lord Krishna.
He was born around 1352 CE, which is quite recent in historical terms:
Around 32 years after the Khilji dynasty ended (1320 CE),
Around 202 years after Qutb-ud-din Aibak (who built the Qutub Minar) passed away in 1210 CE.
This means he lived during a time that’s not considered “mythological,” but well-documented in medieval Indian history.
Only 30 Years on Earth – Yet a Lifetime of Miracles

Baba Ramdev Peer took jivat samadhi (left his body consciously) at the age of just 30 years. But in that short span, he performed far more miracles than both Lord Rama and Lord Krishna combined—even though they lived longer.
In fact, even after his samadhi, people say that he still performs miracles—like healing humans or animals instantly, just by someone calling his name with faith.
That’s the level of power he holds, even from the astral plane.
Why Was He So Powerful Compared to Other Avatars of Vishnu?
Let’s compare:
Lord Rama was born in Treta Yuga.
Lord Krishna was born in Dwapar Yuga.
Baba Ramdev Peer appeared in Kalyug.
Now look at the pattern:
Lord Rama performed fewer miracles.
Lord Krishna did more miracles than Rama.
Baba Ramdev Peer did even more miracles than Krishna—and in a much shorter lifetime.
This shows that with each passing yuga, the divine power of Vishnu’s avatars increased, possibly to match the growing spiritual challenges of each age.
Giving Life After Death – An Extraordinary Power
According to scriptures:
Lord Krishna revived only one person—King Parikshit, while he was still in the womb.
Lord Rama turned Ahilya from a stone back to a woman, but didn’t give life back to anyone.
On the other hand, Baba Ramdev Peer could revive not only humans but also animals, even after his death.
That’s not just spiritual greatness—it’s proof of tremendous astral energy and divine potency in Kalyug.
Speed of Response: A Clear Difference
Let’s say someone is suffering from a minor health issue:
If they call upon Baba Ramdev Peer, it might get resolved in a day.
If they call Lord Krishna, it could take a month.
If they ask Lord Rama, the issue might persist for months or even years.
Why? Because Baba Ramdev Peer is a recent avatar and still actively connected to this age (Kalyug), making him more accessible and faster to respond.
Why It's Important to Worship an Energized Deity and Guru
Let’s first understand the right approach:

A person should worship a “jagrit” (awakened or energized) deity—and that deity is none other than your Kuldevta. Along with this, one must follow a Guru who is also spiritually energized, someone who truly guides you on the path.
But here’s a crucial point:

A Guru cannot be an ordinary human. Why? Because all humans carry the burden of the five vices—kaam, krodh, lobh, moh, and ahankar. A human Guru, no matter how spiritual they appear, will pass on their flaws to the disciple. That’s why your Guru must be a divine or deity-level tattva, not a person.
The Secret Power of Kuldevta
The Kuldevta is not just any deity—they are energized in this Kalyug, and that’s why their power works fast.
No matter what you wish for—spiritual growth, protection, success—it is the Kuldevta who can make it happen, not any random deity you choose to worship.
Why We Use the Names of Lord Ram and Krishna
Now let’s understand an interesting thing:
You might wonder why we chant mantras of Lord Ram or Krishna, especially when there are more recent avatars like Baba Ramdevji.
Here’s why:
The more recent the avatar, the more active and powerful they are in this yuga.
For example, Lord Krishna did 2–4 years of spiritual practice before realizing he was an avatar of Lord Vishnu.
Baba Ramdevji did around 12 years of intense tapasya to become an energized avatar.
But Lord Ram was born already energized. He didn’t need to do any sadhana to awaken his powers. From birth, he knew his divine purpose.
So, the more recent the avatar, the more quickly they got energized—and the more powerful they become in this age.
But What About the Mantras?
This is where most people get confused.
When it comes to avatars, newer is better.
But when it comes to mantras, older is more powerful.
The older the mantra, the more cosmic power it holds.
That’s why the “Tarak Mantra” – RAM is considered the most powerful. You may have heard:
“Ram Naam Satya Hai” – it holds power even after death!
The Real Magic: Combine Oldest Mantra with Newest Avatar
Here’s the secret formula:
If you worship the most recent, energized avatar (like Baba Ramdevji or others from this yug)
with the oldest and most powerful mantra (like “Ram”),
you unlock divine results beyond imagination.
But what most people do is the opposite:
They think, “This Baba is powerful, so his mantra must be too”—and they start chanting it.
But unless the mantra has deep age-old energy, it won’t deliver much.
How an Avatar or Person Becomes “Energized”
What Does “Energized” Mean?

An energized person or avatar is someone who has regained access to all the powerful, subtle (astral) bodies from their previous spiritual lives. These astral bodies carry all the accumulated energy, wisdom, and sadhana (spiritual practice) from past incarnations.
Instead of starting from scratch, such a person calls back these astral bodies and continues their spiritual journey from a much more advanced level.
Example: How Lord Krishna Became Energized
Even Lord Krishna had to reclaim all his previous energized astral bodies to become fully powerful in his avatar. It took him around 2 to 4 years to complete this process.
Here are some of the powerful avatars of Lord Vishnu that came before Krishna, whose subtle bodies became part of Krishna’s energy:
Major Avatars Before Krishna:
Matsya (Fish) – Saved the Vedas and humanity.
Kurma (Tortoise) – Held Mount Mandara during the ocean churning.
Varaha (Boar) – Rescued Mother Earth from a demon.
Narasimha (Man-Lion) – Protected Prahlad and destroyed Hiranyakashipu.
Vamana (Dwarf) – Subdued King Bali with three giant steps.
Parashurama (Warrior Sage) – Eliminated corrupt rulers.
Rama (Ideal King) – Lived a life of dharma and defeated Ravana.
All these subtle bodies became part of Krishna’s spiritual makeup—making him more powerful than any previous avatar.
Baba Ramdev Peer: The Most Energized Avatar?
When Lord Vishnu took the form of Baba Ramdev Peer, he had access to even more powerful astral bodies than Krishna did.
Here’s why:
Before Baba Ramdev Peer, these avatars existed:
Matsya
Kurma
Varaha
Narasimha
Vamana
Parashurama
Rama
Krishna
Buddha
… and many more we don’t even know about!
By the time Baba Ramdev Peer took birth, he carried the power and experience of all previous avatars combined, making him the most powerful avatar in Kalyug.
What This Means for You in Kalyug
Now, here’s the exciting part:
Even though Kalyug is considered the most impure age, a person can become more powerful than ever before. How?
If someone dedicates just 4–5 years to intense spiritual practice,
They can reclaim all their energized astral bodies from past lives, which may number in the thousands or even millions.
The more energized astral bodies a person has, the more powerful they become.
This principle applies not just to spirituality, but to any life path—depending on which “mahasukshma sharir” (subtle energy body) a person aligns with (as explained in Surya Vigyan teachings).
Why Kalyug is Actually Advantageous
Even though Kalyug is filled with negative energies (malinta), it offers a major benefit:
In Satyug, it would take hundreds of years to remove malinta.
But in Kalyug, the same purification can happen in just a few hours.
Why?
Because mantras that have been chanted across multiple yugas have become supercharged with energy. The more ancient the mantra, the more powerful it becomes over time.
Modern Generations = Faster Results

That’s why newer generations are getting faster results in spiritual practices. And even though we have shorter lifespans, we carry more powerful energies—thanks to all our past lives and the availability of ancient mantras.
How Mastery Happens
When you repeatedly engage in a particular type of action or field (spiritual or worldly), you are actually choosing one subtle body over others.
With repetition:
All the past-life subtle bodies associated with that action come together,
Making you energized in that field,
And giving you mastery over it.
Why Not to Worship Ancestors
People often worship their ancestors, but in Ashaeiynn wisdom, this is discouraged. Why?
Your ancestors had different spiritual journeys,
Their astral bodies are not connected to your current path,
So they cannot assist you spiritually.
Instead, you should focus on connecting with your own previous astral bodies, with the help of:
Your Kuldevta (awakened family deity)
Guru Tattva (divine-level Guru energy)
Why Only Kuldevta Can Truly Help You (More Than Other Deities)
In Ashaeiynn’s experience over the past year, we’ve seen something very consistent:
No one’s Kuldevta (ancestral deity) is Lord Ram, Lord Krishna, or even Lord Shiva—despite how divine and powerful they are.
Why?
Because these deities are from earlier yugas (like Treta and Dwapar Yuga), while your Kuldevta is a form of the same divine energy, but energized in this Kalyug—the age we live in now.

For example, Lord Ram and Baba Ramdev Peer are both avatars of Lord Vishnu, but Ramdev Peer is a Kuldevta for many because he was energized in Kalyug, which makes him more accessible and responsive in this era.
The same logic applies to Lord Shiva. His recent manifestations are more likely to be a person’s Kuldevta today, not the ancient Shiva form that was worshipped in earlier yugas.
Why Worshipping Your Kuldevta is So Important
When Lord Vishnu takes birth as an avatar, he gathers all the energetic bodies (astral forms) of his previous lives. This process is called getting energized.
The more recent the avatar, the more powerful they become, because they carry forward all the subtle, powerful forms of their past avatars.
For example:
Lord Krishna took 2–4 years to become fully energized.
Baba Ramdev Peer took 12 years.
But Lord Ram was already energized at birth.
So, by the time Kalki Avatar comes in Kalyug, he’ll carry all of Vishnu’s energies and will be the most powerful of all.
In the same way, your Kuldevta is the most powerful deity for you—because:
They are already energized in Kalyug.
They are specifically connected to your soul’s journey.
They can fulfill your desires faster than other, more popular deities.
Why People Often Worship the Wrong Deity
Let’s take an example.
There’s a famous spiritual place where people go to pray for children. They write their names on stones when their wishes come true.
But here’s the truth:
If those same people had prayed to their own Kuldevta, their wish may have been fulfilled faster and with fewer struggles.
Why don’t they do this?
Because:
They think the famous deity is more powerful.
They don’t even know or respect their own Kuldevta.
They lack guidance from a true Guru Tattva.
The rich and educated often go after fame and popularity.
But the poor and simple still worship their Kuldevta with pure faith—and their wishes come true more easily.
Why? Because they don’t judge by fame; they stay connected to their roots.
What Ashaeiynn Teaches You To Do
Use the one powerful initiated mantra given by Ashaeiynn.
Don’t offer your Kuldevta anything else—no other mantra, no other bhog.
Don’t try to worship your Kuldevta directly—always offer your mantra through our Guru Tattva.
Our Guru Tattva (Shri Hanumanji Maharaj) knows what and when to give to your Kuldevta.
Why is this important?

Because when you worship directly, your pitra (ancestors) may step in. Since they also worshipped the same Kuldevta, they can interfere and cause energetic confusion—you may end up worshipping them instead without realizing.
How to Send Your Mantra to Your Kuldevta (The Right Way)
Only send your mantra to your Kuldevta through the Guru Tattva.
How?
While chanting the mantra, mentally say a prayer: “I offer this mantra to my Guru Tattva. Please offer it to my Kuldevta.”
For new aspirants, offer 10% of your daily mantra to your Kuldevta through this method.
For those fully surrendered to Ashaeiynn, trust the Guru Tattva to handle the offering.
Why We Use Only One Mantra
Ashaeiynn now uses one single mantra for:
Homa
Chanting
Worshipping every deity (including Ganpati, Rameshwar Sarkar, etc.)
Why only one?
So your mantra-doot (spiritual messenger) remains the same.
No new portals open that invite unknown energies.
No confusion or conflict between mantras.
Your mantra shakti (power) grows consistently over time.
This is why we say:
Have one Guru Tattva, one mantra, and one deity (your Kuldevta).
Why Emotions Matter More Than Just Knowledge
Knowledge can make you practical—but only emotions and surrender connect you to the divine.
That’s why true bhakti (devotion) comes from the heart, not the head.
When you’re emotionally connected to your mantra, to your Guru Tattva, and to your Kuldevta:
You unlock the subconscious mind.
You activate real transformation.
You attract grace and blessings beyond logic.
Even when you read about Shri Hanumanji Maharaj, you’ll see—he is not just a god of strength but a bhakt (devotee) whose deep love and surrender made him invincible.
